name: Clarithromycin
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Clarithromycin is cleared by both the liver and the kidneys (20% to 30% unchanged in urine). The US label halves the dose when creatinine clearance (CrCl) is below 30 mL/min, and with atazanavir or ritonavir it halves the dose at CrCl 30–60 and cuts it by 75% below 30. Clarithromycin with colchicine is contraindicated in kidney impairment.
kidney_function_basis: Label uses CrCl (mL/min); bands at 60 and 30.

bands.recommendation: No dose change, unless taking atazanavir or a ritonavir-containing regimen: then reduce by 50% (CrCl 30–60) (label).
CrCl below 30: reduce dose by 50%; with atazanavir or ritonavir-containing regimens, reduce by 75% (label).
CrCl below 30: reduce dose by 50%; with atazanavir or ritonavir-containing regimens, reduce by 75% (label).

hd: No dialysis-specific dose in label; serum levels are not expected to be affected much by hemodialysis (label). The label's CrCl below 30 rule (reduce by 50%) is the closest guidance. Do not combine with colchicine.
pd: No dialysis-specific dose in label; peritoneal dialysis is not expected to remove much (label). The CrCl below 30 rule (reduce by 50%) is the closest guidance.
crrt: Not in label; the cited CRRT review (Li 2020) gives no regimen for this drug. Specialist input.
dialyzable: No: serum levels not expected to be appreciably affected by hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis (label).
monitoring: CrCl for dose; QT interval and potassium/magnesium; liver tests; levels of CYP3A substrates (tacrolimus, cyclosporine, carbamazepine) and digoxin; blood pressure and kidney function with CYP3A-metabolized calcium channel blockers (label).

pediatric.usual_dose: 15 mg/kg/day divided every 12 hours for 10 days; mycobacterial infections 7.5 mg/kg (up to 500 mg) every 12 hours (label).

renal.recommendation: No pediatric kidney dosing in label (the CrCl table is not age-specific). Specialist input.
